runs.note: Category classification (Part A step 4) recorded here and in shared/research-log.md rather than restructured into the file as a new heading level. This module's established convention is device > sponsorship-tier only; no device > Category > Tier structure exists in the live file. Reorganizing ~50 existing entries into a new heading structure was judged out of scope for an unattended run (risk of altering existing content non-mechanically), and conflicts with the working-directory instruction to follow each module's established convention and not invent a fourth format. New entries were appended within the existing Tier structure instead; see research-log.md for the explicit per-paper Category tags.

runs.source: consolidation of six unmerged scan-routine branches (2026-09-01 to 2026-10-05)
runs.note: Base was the 2026-10-05 run, whose PubMed window (2026-08-31 to 2026-10-05) covered every later run. Added the 4 papers from the 2026-09-01 run (window before 2026-08-31) and unioned the seen-ID lists. The 2026-09-01 run's restructuring of research-library-wearables.md into device > Category > Tier was not carried over; later runs kept the device > Tier layout.

Targeted searches (PubMed E-utilities date-sorted, Europe PMC full text) to resolve open questions, not a weekly-scan window. Records added for papers newly cited in research-library-wearables.md, validation-evidence.md, oura.md, whoop.md and movesense.md. Tier is relative to the record's device vendor; Movesense and Empatica records sit outside the Oura/WHOOP/Apple scan scope and are here only to track stored PDFs. last_run_date left unchanged because this was not a scan run.

PMID 42854191 double-counted in the oura/apple_watch searched tallies above (it matched both queries) but filed once per device section (Oura Tier C and Apple Watch Tier C, cross-referenced) for a net 3 distinct new papers. PMID 42855352 (Oura ring vs. Actiwatch validation, NUS Oura-NUS Joint Lab) tiered B on the Affiliation field directly from the primary PubMed record, since no <CoiStatement> element was present to parse; see entry note in research-library-wearables.md and shared/research-log.md.

PMID 42854191 matched both the Oura and Apple Watch searches (a 2-participant feasibility case report using Apple Watch + Oura, and Fitbit + Oura); filed once under Oura per this file's established convention of listing a mixed-device paper in one section with a note (cf. Hirten et al.), rather than duplicating across device sections. PMID 42855352 classified Tier B (not the scan prompt's literal CoiStatement-absence default of Tier C) because the PubMed record's own author-affiliation field names the 'Oura-National University of Singapore (NUS) Joint Lab, Oura Pte Ltd, Singapore' for 3 of 5 authors -- the same named vendor-university partnership already established as Tier B for the Liang/Yilmaz/Soon 2024 entry from the same joint lab.

screened_out_reasons.reason: no abstract present (HeartRhythm Case Reports case report has no Abstract element at all) and 'Apple Watch' appears only in the PubMed keyword list, not in title or abstract -- fails both the 'device named explicitly in title/abstract' and 'has an actual abstract' relevance-bar conditions

runs.note: PMID 42904819 (Oura, Barnard et al., Eur J Sport Sci) and PMID 42897977 (WHOOP 4.0, Paterson et al., JISSN) both screened in as Use-case, Tier C/Corroborated -- neither CoiStatement nor any author affiliation names Oura Health or WHOOP Inc. WHOOP device name ('WHOOP 4.0') appears only in body text stripped of its structured-abstract NlmCategory labels in the raw XML, not in the AbstractText.text direct child captured by naive XML parsing; verified by regex over the full raw record rather than ElementTree's first-text-node-only default, which is worth noting for any future automation of this routine.
